talk.text: Wait. Is there a hole in that roof?
Yep! That's the Pantheon in Rome, and it's almost two thousand years old.
Seriously? And the dome's still standing?
Still the biggest dome ever built in plain concrete. No steel inside at all.

label.name: The coffers
label.meta: Sunken panels that lighten the dome

talk.text: Okay, and what are all those square dents?
They're called coffers. They make the dome lighter, so it can hold itself up.
So what happens when it rains?
(laughs) It rains inside! The floor slopes a little, and drains carry the water away.

outro: No way. Where do I find more like this?
caption:
Wait… is there a hole in that roof? ☔️

The Pantheon in Rome (c. 125 AD) is still the largest dome ever built in unreinforced concrete. Coffers lighten it, and the oculus at the top is open to the sky — when it rains, it rains inside.
